title: `share()` can fail with `MORI_EEXIST` after PID reuse of a crashed process
description:
Region names are `mori_<pid>_<counter>` where `counter` starts at `0` for every process. On Linux/macOS the OS recycles PIDs, so a fresh process can inherit the PID of a process that was killed before cleaning up its SHM.

When that happens, the new process's first `share()` calls regenerate the *exact* names (`mori_<pid>_0`, `mori_<pid>_1`, …) of the orphaned regions left by the dead incarnation. Because `mori_shm_create` opens with `O_EXCL` (POSIX) / checks `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS` (Windows) and never reuses an existing region, this surfaces as an error (`MORI_EEXIST`) rather than silent corruption — but `share()` fails until the orphans are pruned, and the new process cannot reap them itself (it reads its own PID as alive).

**Fix:** start the counter at a per-process random value so PID reuse alone is no longer sufficient to collide — a collision additionally requires a ~2^-32 counter overlap.

title: Request: manual clearup of mori shared objects
description:
Hello, I'm using `mori` and `mirai_map` to run large numbers of calcs without running out of RAM. I'm using a docker container running ubuntu and if for any reason the process gets killed or interrupted or otherwise doesn't conclude properly the shared mori object files get left behind in `/dev/shm/`.  To stop these taking up space and creating problems for the next run I've added a manual step at the start of my script to delete all files in `/dev/shm/` whose names start with `mori_`, but I wonder if there should be a function in the `mori` package that does this for you? My approach is pretty crude and only works because I know where the shared files are going to be (it wouldn't work on Windows, for example). 

On a related note, would it also be useful to have a function that tells you where and with what prefix the mori objects in this session will be saved?  For example if you wanted to clear out mori objects from the current session without interfering with any others.

Or maybe there are better ways to solve these problems?

Session info etc is the same as mentioned in this issue: https://github.com/shikokuchuo/mori/issues/14#issue-4364438661

title: name override?
description:
FANTASTIC package idea!

Would you consider allowing the user to over-ride the name assigned?

Setup: multiple processes in a shiny environment (posit connect), all accessing a few largish datasets. It would be easy for a thin wrapper to look for (say) `mori::map_shared("20260512_table1")` and react if that errs, effectively a relatively built-in cache-filling setup. Since the processes are started automatically from the service supervisor script, we don't have an immediate way to pass the string between processes.

(My particular use-case: in car-racing, we get location and telemetry data frequently, all written to a local- or nfs-mount as parquet files. All processes periodically scan for new files and read in data as it becomes visible. It could be very useful to reduce the "fs-poll" and have it pulled into shared memory just once and reused by all subprocs.)

Other methods:

- load the data into a redis hash and use that, though certainly (de)serialization penalties, and not benefiting from the actual sharing of data
- load the _name_ of the shm share into a redis hash by the keys I want to use, and just react to errors

Side note, perhaps different issues if you think they're worthy, I'm happy submitting separate FRs for them.

- helper function to report the amount of shared memory available; this could just be a `system()` call for `df --block-size=1  /dev/shm` (unix-y) or `sysctl -n hw.memsize` on macos, or `memory.limit()` on windows; not sure if there are _simple_ ways to determine available-vs-used ...
- any way to list available objects in shared memory? or is this too lazy of me, abusing the shm for the wrong reason?

title: Silently returns NA if 'mori' is not available to unserialize
description:
# TL;DR

If a parallel worker does _not_ have **mori** installed, passing a `mori::share()` object will result in missing values. 

Implications: This introduces a risk for silently returning incorrect results in long-running, parallel pipelines, and potentially also under other non-predictable setups that end-users might operate with.


# Reproducible example

```r
library(parallel)

## Set up a cluster worker without 'mori' available
cl <- makeCluster(1L)
void <- clusterEvalQ(cl, .libPaths(tempdir()))
## Assert that 'mori' is not available
res <- clusterEvalQ(cl, requireNamespace("mori"))[[1]]
stopifnot(isFALSE(res))

set.seed(42)
x <- rnorm(1e6)
x_shared <- mori::share(x)

truth <- x_shared[1:3]
str(truth)
#> num [1:3] 1.371 -0.565 0.363
stopifnot(identical(truth, x[1:3]))

clusterExport(cl, "x_shared")
y <- clusterEvalQ(cl, x_shared[1:3])[[1]]
str(y)
#> num [1:3] NA NA NA
stopifnot(identical(y, truth))
#> Error: identical(y, truth) is not TRUE
```

If we skip:

```r
void <- clusterEvalQ(cl, .libPaths(tempdir()))
```

we get the correct results.

title: Fatal error trying to use `mori::share` in docker container
description:

When I try the same code in a docker container I get a fatal error (bash exit code 135) when I try to run `mori::share()`:

> /azp/_work/_temp/b8bab47b-cadc-40aa-ab90-f21696a6a132.sh: line 2: 480574 Bus error               (core dumped)

title: Path-embedded `shared_name()`
description: So we can round trip `map_shared(shared_name(x))`, where `x` is a sub-list or element, not the root.

title: Access full object after share()?
description:
Imagine you do

```r
x <- mori::share(x)
```

and later realize you want to serialize the full object, e.g. `saveRDS(x, file = "x.rds")`. Is that possible? Is there a way to access the "non-shared" object, other than:

```r
y <- unserialize(serialize(x, NULL))
```

I also understand that if I do `x_shared <- mori::share(x)`, then `x` refers to the non-shared version.

PS. This project is fabulous, especially since it is so narrowly and well scoped.

title: `shared_name()` should return the SHM name for sub-lists and elements
description: Currently `is_shared(x)` returns TRUE for sub-lists and elements extracted from a shared list, but `shared_name(x)` returns an empty string for the same objects.
